summary:
With `t` team members, the final group occupies some arc of exactly `t` seats. Each swap can move one member
from outside into a guest's seat inside, so an arc needs as many swaps as it has guests. Slide a window of `t`
seats around the circle (indices modulo `n`) to find the arc with the most members; the answer is `t` minus
that. O(n).

question.md:
Seats form a circle; `1` is a team member, `0` a guest. Any two people can swap seats. Return the fewest swaps to
make all members sit together.

- **n up to 10⁵.**
- The first and last seats are neighbours.

think.md:
`seats = [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1]` → **2** swap(s).

The team has 5 members, so the target is a block of 5 consecutive seats (around the circle). Inside that
block, every guest has to leave and a member from outside has to come in: one swap fixes exactly one such
pair, and nothing does better. So the cost of a block is its number of guests, and we want the block with the
fewest guests, i.e. the most members.

Going around the circle is handled by indexing `i % n`, so the window can wrap past the end.

idea.md: For each start `i`, count members in seats `i, i+1, …, i+t−1` (mod n). Answer: `t − max`.

lines.text: Every arc start around the circle.
Guests in the best arc = swaps needed. No members gives 0.

steps.text: Arc starting at seat 0: 2 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 1: 3 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 2: 2 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 3: 2 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 4: 3 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 5: 3 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 6: 2 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 7: 3 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 8: 3 guest(s) to swap out.
Arc starting at seat 9: 2 guest(s) to swap out.

walk.title: There are 5 team members, so the final group fills some arc of 5 seats. Try each arc and count the guests in it.

limits.md: Neighbouring arcs share `t − 1` seats; recounting them is wasted work.

approaches.title: Circular sliding window

idea.md: Count members in seats `0..t−1`. For `i = t .. n+t−2`: add `seats[i % n]`, drop `seats[(i − t) % n]`; keep the max. Answer `t − max`.

build: Slide around the circle with `% n`.

lines.text: Team size `t`; with nobody to group, no swaps.
Members in the arc of seats `0..t−1`.
Move the arc one seat clockwise: seat `i % n` enters, seat `(i − t) % n` leaves. The loop covers all `n` starting seats.
Every guest in the best arc costs one swap.

steps.text: Window starting at seat 1: add seat 5, drop seat 0 → 2 members.
Window starting at seat 2: add seat 6, drop seat 1 → 3 members.
Window starting at seat 3: add seat 7, drop seat 2 → 3 members.
Window starting at seat 9: add seat 3, drop seat 8 → 3 members.
At most 3 members already sit together, so 5 − 3 = 2 swaps.

walk.title: Slide a window of 5 seats around the circle (index modulo n), keeping the count of members inside.

takeaways.md:
- **Grouping k items** = choose a window of size k; its cost is what doesn't belong inside it.
- **Circular arrays:** let the index run past `n` and use `i % n` (or append the array to itself).
- A swap fixes one misplaced pair, so the cost is the number of outsiders in the window.
